title: Retrospective OMF charges — unreasoned order quashed
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Arindam Sinha and Satya Veer Singh, JJ.
disposition: Impugned order quashed for lack of reasons; Executive Engineer to pass a fresh order on the retrospective claim after the petitioner pays current-bill arrears.
headnote: An Executive Engineer’s order reiterating retrospective electricity charges, made without dealing with the consumer’s objection under clause 5.6 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and the recorded CT ratio/OMF, suffers from lack of reasons and is quashed. A fresh order on the retrospective claim is to follow payment of outstanding current bills.
facts: The petitioner challenged an order dated 6 November 2025 reiterating retrospective electricity charges on bills already paid. A coordinate Bench on 13 August 2025 had directed MRI supply, a hearing, a reasoned order, and no coercive recovery. The petitioner’s 16 September 2025 objection alleged a fresh sealing certificate showing OMF=200 without clause 5.6 compliance, and that the 9 May 2023 certificate recorded CT ratio 10/5 and OMF=2, not 1000/5. The company said the MRI was supplied and the petitioner heard.

holding_units.holding: An order reiterating retrospective charges without dealing with the consumer’s objection—including alleged non-compliance with clause 5.6 (no check meter; MRI not properly supplied) and the sealing-certificate CT ratio/OMF of 10/5 and 2 versus the claimed 1000/5 and 200—suffers from lack of reasons and is set aside. The Executive Engineer must pass a fresh order on the retrospective claim after the consumer pays outstanding arrears on current bills.

not_decided.note: Whether clause 5.6 was complied with (check meter; MRI analysis) before the OMF=200 assessment.
Whether the CT ratio is 1000/5 (OMF 200) or 10/5 (OMF 2) as recorded in the 9 May 2023 sealing certificate.
Merits of the retrospective consumption charges.
